children: Australian shares were little changed on Monday as gains in  mining and energy stocks offset losses in gold stocks, with investors weighing renewed U.S. rate hike expectations and persistently elevated Australian rate hike bets.
ended 0.1% higher at 9,010.90 points. It dropped 1% last week in its steepest weekly slump since mid-August.

The strong U.S. employment report for August on Friday increased bets for a hawkish move at the Federal Reserve's meeting next week, with investor focus now shifting to consumer price inflation data on Friday.

While in Australia, better-than-expected June-quarter GDP data last week boosted expectations of a hike later this month. Swaps imply nearly a 70% chance of a quarter-point increase to 4.6% at the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) monetary policy meeting on September 28–29.
"A dual hawkish stance from the Federal Reserve and RBA would be a headwind for Australian equities," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
"Higher rates on both sides would pressure rate-sensitive sectors such as banks, property and consumer discretionary, while also supporting the Australian dollar."
